citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space, let $Y$ be a dense linear subspace of $H$ that is itself
a Hilbert space continuously embedded in $H$ (for instance $Y=D(A_0)$ with the
graph norm of a self-adjoint $A_0$), let $T>0$, and let $A(t)$ for
$t\in[0,T]$ be an operator with $D(A(t))=Y$, self-adjoint as an operator on $H$,
such that $t\mapsto A(t)$ belongs to $C^1([0,T];\mathcal B(Y,H))$
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Put $L:=\sup_t\|A'(t)\|_{\mathcal B(Y,H)}$.
Then:

(a) *Existence and uniqueness of a strong propagator.* There is a family
$U(t,s)$, $0\le s\le t\le T$, of unitary operators on $H$ with:
$U(s,s)=I$; $U(t,s)U(s,r)=U(t,r)$; $(t,s)\mapsto U(t,s)\xi$ continuous on
$\{s\le t\}$ for each $\xi\in H$; $U(t,s)Y=Y$ with
$\|U(t,s)y\|_Y\le C_T\|y\|_Y$ for a constant $C_T$ independent of
$(s,t)\in[0,T]^2$; and for every $y\in Y$ the map $t\mapsto U(t,s)y$ is $C^1$
in $H$ with
$$i\,\partial_tU(t,s)y=A(t)U(t,s)y,\qquad s\le t\le T.$$

(b) *Uniqueness.* If $V(t,s)$ is another family of bounded linear operators on $H$ with the same strong equation
on $Y$, $V(s,s)=I$ and $\sup_{r}\|V(r,s)y\|_{H}<\infty$, then $V=U$.

(c) *Equations for the reverse and adjoint.* $U(t,s)Y=Y$ for all $0\le s\le t\le T$
and $U(s,t):=U(t,s)^{-1}$ satisfies $i\partial_sU(s,t)y=A(s)U(s,t)y$ for
$y\in Y$; $U(t,s)^*=U(s,t)$. Equivalently, differentiating the second
argument of the forward propagator gives $i\partial_sU(t,s)y=-U(t,s)A(s)y$.
The domain maps are jointly strongly continuous in $Y$.

The theorem is stated for the abstract family $A$; a physical generator is
obtained by $A=H_{\mathrm{energy}}/\hbar$ after choosing a time unit.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$m,\omega,\hbar>0$, let $\ell:=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, let
$H_{\mathrm{osc}}=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}DAD^{-1}$ be the oscillator of
[[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] with
orthonormal eigenbasis $(\psi_n)_{n\ge0}$ and ladder operators
$a_\psi,a_\psi^\dagger,N_\psi$ of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]]
transported to $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$. Work with $\langle u,v\rangle=\int u\overline v$, linear in its first argument, and define $N_\psi^{1/2}$ by the coefficient action $\sqrt n\,c_n$ on $D(N_\psi^{1/2})=\{\psi:\sum_n n|c_n|^2<\infty\}$, where $c_n=\langle\psi,\psi_n\rangle$. Use the negative-sign $2\pi$ Fourier convention $\widehat u(\xi)=\int e^{-2\pi i x\xi}u(x)\,dx$ on integrable inputs and its Plancherel extension $\mathcal F_2$. Let
$Q=M_x$, $P=\mathcal F_2^*M_{2\pi\hbar\xi}\mathcal F_2$ be the maximal
position and momentum operators (their self-adjointness is proved below), with
$D(Q)=\{\psi:x\psi\in L^2\}$ and
$D(P)=\{\psi:\xi\mathcal F_2\psi\in L^2\}$, with
$H_{\mathrm{osc}}=\hbar\omega(N_\psi+\frac12I)$ and the couplings
$$Q=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}(a_\psi+a_\psi^\dagger),\qquad P=\frac{\hbar}{i\ell\sqrt2}(a_\psi-a_\psi^\dagger)$$
on the common domain $D(N_\psi^{1/2})$. Let $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ be of class
$C^1$. Put $Y:=D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})=D(N_\psi)$ with graph norm
$\|\psi\|_Y^2:=\|\psi\|^2+\|H_{\mathrm{osc}}\psi\|^2$. Then:

(a) *Ladder bounds.* For every $\psi\in D(N_\psi^{1/2})$,
$$\|Q\psi\|\le\ell\bigl(2\|N_\psi^{1/2}\psi\|^2+\|\psi\|^2\bigr)^{1/2},\qquad \|P\psi\|\le\frac{\hbar}{\ell}\bigl(2\|N_\psi^{1/2}\psi\|^2+\|\psi\|^2\bigr)^{1/2}.$$

(b) *Infinitesimal bound.* For every $\eta>0$ there is $b_\eta<\infty$ with
$\|Q\psi\|\le\eta\|H_{\mathrm{osc}}\psi\|+b_\eta\|\psi\|$ for
$\psi\in Y=D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$; hence $-f(t)Q$ is
$H_{\mathrm{osc}}$-bounded with relative bound $0$ for every fixed $t$
([[def-relative-boundedness-with-respect-to-an-operator]]).

(c) *Common domain.* For every $t\in[a,b]$ the operator
$H(t):=H_{\mathrm{osc}}-f(t)Q$ is self-adjoint on the single domain $Y$
(independent of $t$); moreover $t\mapsto H(t)$ belongs to
$C^1([a,b];\mathcal B(Y,L^2))$ with derivative $-f'(t)Q$, so the family has a
common domain and satisfies the regularity hypothesis of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-common-domain-nonautonomous-evolution]].

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) for a declared system, in the state, sharp-observable and evolution readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; units are those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The readings below are the reading of clause (iv) of P4 for the page's models; clause (iv) records that a prescribed time-dependent family is **a different model assumption** from the autonomous one, and clause (b) below adopts it.

**(b) Prescribed energy family.** As an additional model assumption of the pair, fix a nonempty compact interval $I=[a,b]\subset\mathbb R$ of physical times (seconds), the declared state space $\mathfrak H$ of the system, a value $\hbar>0$ of the reduced Planck constant as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and a **prescribed family** $t\mapsto H(t)$ of self-adjoint operators on $\mathfrak H$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]) in one of the following three **regularity classes**, whose hypotheses are part of the model declaration:

- **(i) Bounded norm-continuous class.** $D(H(t))=\mathfrak H$ for every $t$; each $H(t)\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is self-adjoint ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]); $t\mapsto H(t)$ is norm-continuous on $I$ ([[def-operator-norm]]); and $K:=\sup_{t\in I}\|H(t)\|/\hbar<\infty$.
- **(ii) Bounded-control class.** $H(t)=H_{0}+V(t)$, where $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(H_{0})\subseteq\mathfrak H$ and $V:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and $\|V(t)\|=v(t)$, $v:=\sup_{t\in I}v(t)<\infty$.
- **(iii) Common-domain class.** There is a dense linear subspace $Y\subseteq\mathfrak H$ that is itself a Hilbert space continuously embedded in $\mathfrak H$ ([[def-hilbert-space]], for instance $Y=D(H_{0})$ with the graph norm of a self-adjoint $H_{0}$), with $D(H(t))=Y$ for every $t$, each $H(t)$ self-adjoint as an operator on $\mathfrak H$, and $t\mapsto H(t)$ of class $C^{1}(I;\mathcal B(Y,\mathfrak H))$.

The family, its class and its data are **prescribed**: no field equation, source model, back-reaction or feedback of the system on the source is assumed, and no claim is made that any laboratory arrangement realizes the family. The family is coupled to the system through the material hypotheses of the page or of the item that declares a specific model (for instance a magnetic-moment or electric-dipole coupling, or the external-source Coulomb family of the page's adiabatic models); the reading of $H(t)$ as the energy of the declared system is a model assumption.

**(c) The model's evolution.** The **driven model** declares that the time evolution of the system between times $s,t\in I$ is carried by a family $U(t,s)$ of unitary operators on $\mathfrak H$ with
$$U(s,s)=I,\qquad U(t,r)=U(t,s)U(s,r)\quad(r,s,t\in I),\qquad U(t,s)^{*}=U(s,t),$$
jointly strongly continuous in $(t,s)$, solving the time-dependent Schroedinger equation on $I$ in the sense of the class:
in class (i) $U$ is the unique norm-continuous solution of $i\hbar\partial_tU(t,s)=H(t)U(t,s)$ with $U(s,s)=I$ constructed by the Dyson series of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-norm-dyson-series-and-uniqueness]] (whose hypothesis is exactly the norm-continuity of the bounded self-adjoint family);
in class (ii) $U$ is the mild propagator constructed in [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]], satisfying $U(t,s)\psi=E(t-s)\psi-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_s^tE(t-r)V(r)U(r,s)\psi\,dr$ for every $\psi\in\mathfrak H$, with $E(u)=e^{-iuH_{0}/\hbar}$ the autonomous flow of clause (b) of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]];
in class (iii) $U$ is the strong propagator of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-common-domain-nonautonomous-evolution]] with physical generator $A=H/\hbar$, preserving $Y$, for which $t\mapsto U(t,s)y$ is $C^1$ in $\mathfrak H$ with $i\hbar\partial_tU(t,s)y=H(t)U(t,s)y$ for every $y\in Y$.
In each class the cited item is what makes the declaration well posed: it constructs the family and proves uniqueness under the class hypotheses. The model asserts nothing beyond those hypotheses; in particular it asserts no invariant domain and no strong equation for $H_{0}$-domain vectors in class (ii), and no common domain in classes (i) and (ii).

On a singleton interval $I=\{a\}$, the evolution declaration consists only of $U(a,a)=I$; all differential assertions in these class readings apply only when $a<b$, with one-sided derivatives at the endpoints.

**(d) State and outcome readings.** The **evolved preparation** at time $t$ of a preparation $\rho$ specified at time $s$ is $\rho(t):=U(t,s)\rho(s)U(t,s)^{*}$; it is a preparation of the model in the sense of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] for every $t$, by unitarity of $U(t,s)$ and [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]. A pure preparation $[\psi(s)]$ evolves to the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$ with $\psi(t):=U(t,s)\psi(s)\ne0$. The **outcome law at time $t$** of an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]) in that preparation is $\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}$, the reading of P2; the definition records the timing convention once and asserts nothing about how or when a record is produced.

**(e) Energy-basis amplitudes and level populations.** In class (ii), let $(\varphi_{j})_{j\in J}$ be an orthonormal family in $D(H_{0})$ with $H_{0}\varphi_{j}=E_{j}\varphi_{j}$ and $E_{j}\in\mathbb R$ (a complete orthonormal family of eigenvectors is not assumed here). For $s\le t$ and labels $i,j$ the **transition amplitude from $i$ at time $s$ to $j$ at time $t$** is the scalar
$$A_{ji}(t,s):=e^{iE_{j}(t-s)/\hbar}\,\bigl\langle U(t,s)\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\bigr\rangle ,$$
and the **transition probability** is $p_{ji}(t,s):=|A_{ji}(t,s)|^{2}$. If additionally $E_{j}$ is a simple eigenvalue of $H_{0}$ with spectral projection $P_{j}=E_{H_{0}}(\{E_{j}\})$ onto $\mathbb C\varphi_{j}$, then the definition *states*, as the reading of P2, the identity
$$p_{ji}(t,s)=\mu^{H_{0}}_{\psi(t)}(\{E_{j}\})=\|E_{H_{0}}(\{E_{j}\})\psi(t)\|^{2},\qquad \psi(t)=U(t,s)\varphi_{i},$$
which follows from the rank-one form of $P_{j}$ and the normalization $\|\varphi_{j}\|=1$; $p_{ji}$ is the reading of the outcome probability of the value $E_{j}$ of the assigned energy observable $(H_{0},\mathrm J)$ in the evolved preparation, and it is a property of the declared model, not a measured frequency.

**(f) Declared two-level drive models.** Let $(\sigma_{x},\sigma_{y},\sigma_{z})$ be the Pauli matrices of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e) acting on $\mathbb C^{2}$ in the orthonormal basis $(e_{\uparrow},e_{\downarrow})$ ([[def-inner-product-space]]), let $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1},\omega\in\mathbb R$, and put $H_{0}:=\frac{\hbar}{2}\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}$ (class (i) with $I$ any compact interval). The **circular two-level drive model** is the class-(i) family
$$H_{\mathrm c}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\Bigl(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\bigl(\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x}+\sin(\omega t)\sigma_{y}\bigr)\Bigr),$$
and the **linear two-level drive model** is the class-(i) family
$$H_{\mathrm l}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x}\bigr).$$
The real parameters $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1},\omega$ represent angular frequencies of dimension duration$^{-1}$, read in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$; their numerical values are expressed in that unit, so $\omega t$ is dimensionless and $\hbar\omega_{0}$ and $\hbar\Omega_{1}$ have energy units; $\omega_{0}$ is the **splitting frequency** of the model (the level gap is $\hbar|\omega_{0}|$), $\omega$ the **drive frequency**, $\Omega_{1}$ the **transverse coupling**, and $\Delta:=\omega_{0}-\omega$ the **detuning**. Populations of the level pair are the diagonal entries $\langle P_{\bullet}\psi,\psi\rangle$ of the orthogonal projections $P_{\uparrow},P_{\downarrow}$ onto $\mathbb Ce_{\uparrow},\mathbb Ce_{\downarrow}$ in the evolved vector $\psi(t)$. The two families are model data: no identification with a laboratory spin, molecule or field, and no relation of $\Omega_{1}$ to a field amplitude, is asserted; such an identification is a tested identification in the sense of P7.

**(g) Status and scope.** Clauses (b), (c), (f) are adopted model assumptions and readings; the existence and uniqueness of the propagator in each class is cited mathematics, not a consequence of P1, P2 or P4. The model asserts no open-system or environment coupling, no non-unitary reduced dynamics, no measurement or apparatus model, no thermalization or equilibration, no long-time limit and no empirical record; the identification of the family's parameters with laboratory fields and of the system with a laboratory sample is made, if at all, only in separately declared models with their own uncertainty.

**(a) Adopted framework assumptions.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, in the readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]], [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix real model parameters $m>0$ (mass parameter, unit $\mathrm{kg}$), $\omega>0$ (angular frequency, unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$) and the action constant $\hbar>0$ (unit $\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$) of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)4, and put
$$\ell:=\sqrt{\frac{\hbar}{m\omega}}>0\qquad\text{(unit }\mathrm m\text{),}$$
the model's length scale.

**(b) One-dimensional realization.** Write $\mathcal H_1:=L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx;\mathbb C)$ for the model's one-dimensional state space, the complex Hilbert space of almost-everywhere classes with inner product linear in the first argument, taken in the scalar reading $r=1$ of the component-valued space of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] for $d=1$. The model's **position** and **momentum** are the operators of that lemma at $d=1$, $r=1$, namely
$$Q:=M_x,\qquad D(Q)=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:xf\in L^{2}\},\qquad (Qf)(x)=xf(x),$$
$$P:=-i\hbar D_x,\qquad D(P)=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:\text{the weak derivative }D_xf\text{ lies in }L^{2}\},\qquad Pf=-i\hbar D_xf,$$
which are densely defined and self-adjoint with exactly these domains; the model assigns to $(Q,\mathrm m)$ and to $(P,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$ the status of assigned sharp observables in the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), with outcome laws read from P2.

**(c) Energy and excitation-number observables.** Let $g_0,(g_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ and the unitary $D:L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)\to L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$ be the Hermite data and scaling map of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (a), (b) for the parameters $m,\omega,\hbar$. Put $\mathscr P_y:=\{p g_0:p\in\mathbb C[y]\}\subseteq L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$; the Hermite recurrence [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-recurrence]] identifies this polynomial-Gaussian space with $\operatorname{span}\{g_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$, and its scaled image $\mathscr P_x:=D(\mathscr P_y)=\operatorname{span}\{\psi_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$ is the core supplied by the scaling theorem. Let $A$ be the diagonal operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]] for the family $(g_n)$ and eigenvalues $2n+1$. The model's **energy operator** is
$$H_1:=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\,D A D^{-1},\qquad D(H_1):=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:D^{-1}f\in D(A)\},$$
the operator of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clause (b); its exact domain, action, spectrum and eigenbasis are those established there. The model assigns to $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ the status of assigned energy observable of the isolated system in the sense of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clauses (a) and (b): the model's flow is $U(t)=\exp(-itH_1/\hbar)$ and the model's Schroedinger dynamics is the one of that definition. Let $N$ be the self-adjoint number operator on $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$ of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]] for the Hermite family $(g_n)$, and set $N_\psi:=DND^{-1}$. Its transported domain and action are
$$D(N_\psi)=\Bigl\{f\in\mathcal H_1:\sum_n n^2|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad N_\psi f=\sum_n n\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\psi_n,$$
with the series converging in $\mathcal H_1$; it is self-adjoint by [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-unitary-transport-of-spectral-pvms]] clauses (a), (d). The model assigns to $(N_\psi,1)$ the status of its dimensionless excitation-number observable; here $1$ is the dimensionless unit, and the spectral coordinate $n$ records the number of excitations, and its outcome laws are read by P2. On the scaled polynomial-Gaussian core $\mathscr P_x$ the operator $H_1$ is the self-adjoint realization of the quadratic expression: for every $f\in\mathscr P_x$,
$$H_1f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}f''+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}f$$
pointwise, and for every $f\in D(H_1)$ the weak identity $\int (H_1f)\varphi\,dx=\int f\bigl(-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\varphi''+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}\varphi\bigr)dx$ holds for every $\varphi\in C_c^{\infty}(\mathbb R)$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (c), (d)). The formal differential expression $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\frac{d^{2}}{dx^{2}}+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}$ is the model's **quadratic potential energy plus kinetic energy** reading; no identification of $D(H_1)$ with any independently defined maximal differential-operator domain, and no separate quadratic-form-domain characterization, is asserted.

**(d) Three-dimensional isotropic realization.** For the spinless reading $s=0$ of the massive-particle model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]], with state space $\mathcal H_3:=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dx;\mathbb C)$, position operators $Q_j$ and momentum operators $P_k$ ($j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$) with the domains and units of that definition, the model with common frequency $\omega$ has **energy operator** $H_3$ equal to the diagonal operator $H$ of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-multidimensional-oscillator-completeness]] clause (c) for $d=3$, $m_j=m$, $\omega_j=\omega$, a self-adjoint operator on $\mathcal H_3$ with the domain, spectrum and core displayed there. The model assigns to $(H_3,\mathrm J)$ the status of assigned energy observable in the reading of clause (c); its eigenbasis and the identity $H_3=\sum_{j=1}^{3}\bigl(-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\partial_{x_j}^{2}+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x_j^{2}\bigr)$ on the core are those of that theorem, and the one-dimensional realization of clauses (b) and (c) is the coordinate specialization of this one.

**(e) Physical reading and scope.** Clause (c) defines the model quantities that the page calls the energy and excitation number; it is a **model assumption** that the energy of the declared isolated particle is the assigned observable $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ and that $(N_\psi,1)$ is its excitation-number observable. The additive constant of the potential energy is removed at the minimum: for a one-dimensional potential-energy function $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^2$, with values in joules for position $x$ in metres, suppose $V$ has a non-degenerate local minimum at $0$, meaning $V'(0)=0$ and $V''(0)>0$. Taylor's theorem gives $V(x)-V(0)=\frac{1}{2}V''(0)x^{2}+o(x^{2})$ as $x\to0$; the oscillator model approximates this shifted potential-energy function by its quadratic term and sets $m\omega^{2}=V''(0)$. The oscillator's quantum ground energy in this convention is $\hbar\omega/2$. With only the stated $C^2$ regularity, the remainder is $o(x^2)$; no quantitative finite-amplitude error bound is asserted on this page (Binney §3.1, cited in the references). No measured value, no laboratory identification and no derivation of $m$ or $\omega$ from any microscopic or environmental theory is asserted. The model contains no damping, no external driving, no time-dependent parameters, no coupling to electromagnetic fields or radiation, no spin-dependent force, no anharmonic term, no relativistic correction and no boundary or many-body effect; those are separate model assumptions belonging to their own items. The parameters $m$ and $\omega$ are model parameters of dimensions $\mu$ and $\tau^{-1}$ in the conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and all displayed quantities are read in the units fixed there.

**(f) Status.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the objects used by the theorems of this page and record the readings of P1, P2, P4 and P5 in the model's terminology. They assert no preparation or apparatus model, no detection model, no joint outcome law of position and momentum and no empirical result.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework, for systems in the declared massive-matter sector, the following statements about states and their composition. Assume throughout the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), which is the choice hypothesis of the mathematical suppliers cited below.

**(i) State space.** To each physical system of the sector the model assigns a complex Hilbert space $H$ that is nonzero and separable: a complex Hilbert space in the sense of [[def-hilbert-space]] which admits a sequence whose range is dense in $H$, so that the hypothesis of [[thm-separable-hilbert-space-has-a-countable-orthonormal-basis]] holds and $H$ has a finite or countable orthonormal basis. The assignment of a Hilbert space to a physical system is a model assumption; the linear structure used to combine descriptions mathematically is not an empirical claim. The physical system to which $H$ is assigned, and the sector in which the assignment is made, are declared with it.

**(ii) Pure preparations.** A **pure preparation** of the system is a unit ray $[\psi]=\{z\psi:z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\}$ of a vector $\psi\in H$ with $\|\psi\|=1$; that is, two nonzero vectors describe the same pure preparation exactly when they differ by a nonzero complex factor. The zero vector is not a state and no preparation is assigned to it: the normalization $\|\psi\|=1$ is part of the assignment. The ray allows arbitrary nonzero rescaling; between unit representatives the factor has modulus one and is a **global phase**, which has no observable consequence (P2). The rank-one operator $T_{\psi,\psi}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] is the density operator associated with the ray of $\psi$.

**(iii) General preparations and mixing.** A general preparation of the system is a **density operator**: a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ on $H$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)). Pure preparations are the special case $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ with $\|\psi\|=1$. A **statistical mixture** of preparations $\rho_{n}$ with weights $w_{n}\ge0$, $\sum_{n}w_{n}=1$, is the trace-norm convergent sum $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}$ as follows directly in the trace-class Banach space ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]): each density has trace norm one, so $\sum_n\|w_n\rho_n\|_1=1$ gives trace-norm convergence. Every partial sum is positive; operator-norm convergence preserves its nonnegative quadratic forms, and continuity of trace gives $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). Thus the limit is again a density operator, without requiring the components to be orthogonal pure states. The weights are a classical preparation uncertainty and are not amplitudes. Distinct weighted ensembles of pure states may define the same $\rho$.

**(iv) Composition.** Two independent distinguishable subsystems with state spaces $H_{A}$ and $H_{B}$ are composed by the completed Hilbert tensor product $H_{A}\widehat\otimes H_{B}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. Product preparations $\psi_{A}\otimes\psi_{B}$ are simple tensors and are the special case in which each subsystem has its own specified preparation. Their finite linear span is dense in $H_{A}\widehat\otimes H_{B}$ by the construction; a pure composite preparation may be any unit ray in this completion, including a norm limit of finite linear combinations of product vectors, and need not factor. General composite preparations are density operators on this space and include the statistical mixtures of clause (iii). A quantity of subsystem $A$ alone is represented on the composite by an operator of the form $A\otimes I_{B}$ and a quantity of $B$ alone by $I_{A}\otimes B$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] (bounded case; unbounded local operators are treated where they occur). The existence of the completed tensor product is mathematics; the assignment of that product to a composite physical system is the physical assumption here.

**(v) Restrictions that are separate assumptions.** Restrictions of the state space by superselection rules, identical-particle symmetry sectors, and the replacement of the tensor product by more general algebraic structures are not consequences of the clauses above: where such a restriction is used it is adopted separately, and the identical-species sectors are the subject of the postulate P6 of this page.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model within its declared sector. They are not derived from experiment, and they do not assert that a physical system is exactly described by such a Hilbert space; no numerical measurement is recorded. The compatibility of the framework with observation is a question about fully specified models and reported data, in the sense of P7.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following statements about sharp and unsharp real-valued quantities. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The latter is the explicit hypothesis used to obtain the spectral PVM of a general self-adjoint operator from [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] in clause (ii); consumers invoking this construction inherit it.

**(i) Sharp observables.** An **ideal sharp real-valued quantity** (observable) of a system with state space $H$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), meaning $D(A)=D(A^*)$ and $A\psi=A^*\psi$ on this common domain, together with a declared unit in which its real spectral coordinate is read; the unit is part of the assignment, and no numerical value of the coordinate is asserted by the assignment. Symmetry of $A$ on a small domain is not sufficient for self-adjointness, and the domain is a declared part of the observable.

**(ii) Spectral probability.** Let $E_{A}$ be the spectral projection-valued measure of the self-adjoint operator $A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$ and a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ the **probability of the outcome in $B$** is
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_{A}(B)\bigr),\qquad\text{and for a pure preparation }[\psi]\text{ it is }\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}.$$
By clause (b) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] the assignment $B\mapsto\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$ is a probability measure on the Borel sets ([[def-probability-measure]], [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). It is the general form of the Born rule adopted here.

**(iii) Nature of the outcome law.** The probability law is a measure, not necessarily a density with respect to Lebesgue measure and not necessarily a finite or countable sum of point masses: a self-adjoint operator with continuous spectrum ordinarily has no normalizable eigenvector at a point of its continuous spectrum, so an "exact value" of a continuum quantity is not represented by a normalized state. An ideal point value is an idealization; a real detector reports a finite-resolution outcome, that is, the probability of a declared Borel set $B$ such as a bin, and the recorded-event probability is that of (ii) for the bin, not the value of a density at a point.

**(iv) Unsharp finite outcomes.** Outcomes of a finite-resolution apparatus with finitely many channels are described, when the idealization uses bounded effects, by a finite family $(F_{a})_{a=1}^{p}$ of effects on $H$ as defined above, with $\sum_aF_a=I$. The **outcome probabilities** are $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$. They are normalized for every state space assigned by P1, as shown by the preceding general-$H$ calculation. This unsharp extension is an operational description tied to an apparatus model; it is not obtained from the sharp observable by mathematical manipulation alone, and the effects alone do not determine what happens to the state after the outcome (P3).

**(v) Moments are a separate matter.** Statements about the mean, variance or higher moments of the outcome law require the corresponding integrability of $t\mapsto t^{n}$ against $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ and are not part of this postulate; where they are used they are stated with their hypotheses. In particular the existence of $\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$ for an unbounded $A$ is not asserted.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model. They assert nothing about which quantities of a concrete apparatus are sharp, about the physical mechanism producing an outcome or about the completeness of the description; a laboratory record is a classical event whose relation to the model is a tested identification with uncertainty, in the sense of P7.

**(a) Dimensions.** Write $\ell$, $\tau$, $\mu$, $\vartheta$ for the four independent dimension symbols of length, duration, mass and electric charge. A **dimension** is an element of $\mathbb Q^{4}$, written $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ with $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb Q$; products and inverses of dimensions are componentwise addition and negation, and the dimensionless dimension $\ell^{0}\tau^{0}\mu^{0}\vartheta^{0}$ is abbreviated $1$. The conventions assign to each quantity of the framework a dimension $[X]$, subject to $[XY]=[X][Y]$, $[X/Y]=[X][Y]^{-1}$ and $[dX/du]=[X][u]^{-1}$, with sums meaningful only between quantities of equal dimension, in which case the sum carries that dimension. For a rational power $q$, dimension powers mean $[X]^q=\ell^{qa}\tau^{qb}\mu^{qc}\vartheta^{qd}$ when $[X]=\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$. Rational exponents include the half-integer wave-function dimensions in clause (d); the integer-exponent dimensions form the subgroup $\mathbb Z^4$. These are consistency requirements on the conventions, not laws of nature.

For extensions using temperature, adjoin an independent dimension symbol $\Theta$: the enlarged group is $\mathbb Q^4\times\mathbb Q$, written $\ell^a\tau^b\mu^c\vartheta^d\Theta^e$, with the same componentwise rules. The preceding group embeds by $e=0$, so all previously assigned dimensions are preserved. Temperature has dimension $\Theta$, the Boltzmann constant has dimension $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-2}\Theta^{-1}$, and entropy in joules per kelvin has that same dimension; a dimensionless entropy remains dimensionless. This convention does not assign a temperature or an entropy to any system.

**(b) Reference units.** The **metre** (m), **second** (s), **kilogram** (kg) and **coulomb** (C) are the reference units of length, duration, mass and charge; a quantity of dimension $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ is expressed in the unit $\mathrm m^{a}\mathrm s^{b}\mathrm kg^{c}\mathrm C^{d}$. Coordinates of an inertial frame are read with the time coordinate $t$ in seconds, $[t]=\tau$, and the spatial coordinates $x_{i}$ in metres, $[x_{i}]=\ell$; slice distances of the arena are read in metres. In the temperature extension the reference unit of $\Theta$ is the kelvin (K), so the general reference unit gains a factor $\mathrm K^e$.

**(c) Defining constants of the current SI.** The framework keeps $\hbar$ explicit. In the current SI the constants $h$, $c$ and $e$ are exact defining constants, with the values $h=6{,}626\,070\,15\times10^{-34}$ J s, $c=2{,}99792458\times10^{8}$ m s$^{-1}$ and $e=1{,}602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}$ C, and $\hbar:=h/(2\pi)$. These are real scalar constants with dimensions and units $[h]=[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$ (J s), $[c]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ (m s$^{-1}$), and $[e]=\vartheta$ (C). The vacuum permeability $\mu_{0}$ is a positive real scalar that is experimentally determined in the current SI, with $[\mu_{0}]=\mu\ell\vartheta^{-2}$ (N A$^{-2}$ = H m$^{-1}$); $\varepsilon_{0}:=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1}$ is a positive real scalar with $[\varepsilon_{0}]=\mu^{-1}\ell^{-3}\tau^{2}\vartheta^{2}$ (F m$^{-1}$). These are unit-convention statements of the SI, not measurements reported by this framework; $c$ enters the framework only through the separate radiation assumptions adopted on their own pages, not in the nonrelativistic spacetime of [[def-nrqm-framework-newtonian-spacetime]].

**(d) Dimensions and types of the framework's quantities.** The dimension map is fixed on the following quantities.

1. State quantities: a position wave function of a system with $d$ spatial dimensions and $r$ internal components is an almost-everywhere equivalence class in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with dimension $\ell^{-d/2}$, its norm $\|\psi\|$ is dimensionless, and an abstract normalized state and the density operators of the state postulate are dimensionless.
2. Probability: the outcome probability $\mu(B)$ of the observable postulate is a dimensionless number; a position density $|\psi|^{2}$ has dimension $\ell^{-d}$; a momentum wave function normalized against $\mathrm d^{d}p$ has dimension $(\mu\ell\tau^{-1})^{-d/2}$; an amplitude for a finite outcome is a dimensionless complex number, while an amplitude read against a detector coordinate carries the square-root of the inverse of the detector measure.
3. Frame parameters ([[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]]): $[b]=\tau$, $[a_{i}]=\ell$, $[v_{i}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ and $[R_{ij}]=1$.
4. Mechanical quantities: action $[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; energy and the Hamiltonian eigenvalues $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$; momentum $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$; position components $\ell$; angular momentum and spin $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; mass $\mu$; velocity of a free spinless model $\ell\tau^{-1}$; force $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$; a real potential energy $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$.
5. Probability current: in the ordinary continuous-field regime, fix an integer $d\ge1$, an open spatial region $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ and an open time interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$. A **probability current density** is a declared continuous map $j:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^d$, whose spatial components have dimension $\ell^{1-d}\tau^{-1}$ and reference unit $\mathrm m^{1-d}\mathrm s^{-1}$. At fixed time it is a spatial vector field; its signed normal component is read as probability transported per unit spatial $(d-1)$-area and time. Explicitly, for a flat face $S=\{x:x_k=a,\ a_i\le x_i\le b_i\ (i\ne k)\}\subset\Omega$, with $a_i<b_i$ and chosen normal $n=\epsilon e_k$, $\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}$, define its **signed probability flux** at $t\in I$ as $\Phi_S(t):=\epsilon\int_{\prod_{i\ne k}[a_i,b_i]}j_k(x_1,\ldots,x_{k-1},a,x_{k+1},\ldots,x_d,t)\prod_{i\ne k}dx_i$. Here $e_k$ is the $k$th coordinate unit vector and the integral uses $(d-1)$-dimensional Lebesgue measure; for $d=1$ this means $\Phi_{\{a\}}(t)=\epsilon j(a,t)$. The flux has dimension $\tau^{-1}$ and unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$; positive sign means transport in the chosen normal direction. Fluxes through curved surfaces, or currents with weaker regularity, require separately specified surface measures or traces. This fixes the quantity type and flux convention; it supplies neither a current associated to an arbitrary $L^2$ state nor a conservation or detector law. Each dynamical model supplies its current construction and balance hypotheses.
6. Electric quantities of the model parameters: charge has dimension $\vartheta$; a magnetic moment has dimension $\ell^{2}\vartheta\tau^{-1}$, equivalently $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{2}=\mathrm J\,\mathrm T^{-1}$, and a gyromagnetic parameter $\gamma$ in the relation $\boldsymbol\mu=\gamma\mathbf S$ has dimension $\mu^{-1}\vartheta$, equivalently $\mathrm s^{-1}\mathrm T^{-1}$; these quantities appear only in the model assumptions that introduce them.
7. Statistical quantities: a mean has the dimension of its outcome coordinate, a variance the square of it and a standard deviation it; a mean, variance or higher moment exists only when the corresponding moment of the outcome probability is finite, so a symbolic average is not a number unless that integrability is established. Angles and phases are dimensionless under the radian convention.
8. Quantities of later extension assumptions - radiation frequencies and energies, electric dipole moments, cross sections, temperatures and entropies - are declared with their dimensions and units by the items that introduce those assumptions, under the rules fixed here; they are not part of the present list.

**(e) Conventions only.** No numerical value of any model parameter is fixed by this item: no mass, charge, spin label, potential or measured constant is asserted, and natural-unit shorthand (for example setting $\hbar=1$ or $c=1$) is read as an abbreviation for the corresponding SI-dimensioned statement with the constant restored.

derivations.claim: [Well-posedness] If $a=b$, set $U(a,a)=I$; the domain, norm and continuity assertions hold with $C_I=1$, and no derivative is asserted under the model's singleton convention. For $a<b$, the generator family $A(t)=H(t)/\hbar$ has $D(A(t))=Y$ for every $t$, is self-adjoint on $H$ as a scalar multiple of $H(t)$, and belongs to $C^{1}(I;\mathcal B(Y,H))$ with $A'(t)=H'(t)/\hbar$ and $\sup_t\|A'(t)\|_{\mathcal B(Y,H)}=L/\hbar<\infty$; these are exactly the hypotheses of [F1] with $T=b-a$ and the time reparametrisation $t\mapsto t-a$, so [F1] supplies the family $U$ with all displayed properties and identifies it with the model's clause (c)(iii). For explicit dependence, put $K(t)=A(t)-i:Y\to\mathfrak H$, $M=\sup_t\|K(t)^{-1}\|_{\mathfrak H\to Y}$, $N=\sup_t\|K(t)\|_{Y\to\mathfrak H}$, and $L_A=L/\hbar$. The bounded inverse and local Neumann construction in [F1], shows $M,N<\infty$ on compact $I$, without a further hypothesis. Its frozen-product construction bounds the frozen products and limiting evolution in $Y$ by a uniform constant controlled by $MN e^{L_A M(b-a)}$, with the endpoint graph conversions described there. Thus the genuine family-dependent graph constants, rather than $I,L$ alone, control $C_I$. This is clause (a).

[Reverse and adjoint equations] For $a=b$, clause (b) reduces to the identity and continuity of $U(a,a)=I$. For $a<b$, the second and third assertions of [F1] give $U(t,s)^{*}=U(s,t)$ and $i\hbar\partial_{s}U(t,s)y=-U(t,s)H(s)y$ for $y\in Y$ after multiplying by $\hbar$, together with the joint strong continuity of the domain maps in the graph norm of $Y$. This is clause (b).

[The driven oscillator is an instance] By [F2], $H(t)=H_{\mathrm{osc}}-f(t)Q$ is self-adjoint on the single domain $Y$ for every $t$ and the family is of class $C^{1}(I;\mathcal B(Y,L^{2}))$ with derivative $-f'(t)Q$; this is precisely the common-domain class hypothesis of the model's clause (b)(iii) with $\mathfrak H=L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$ and the declared reading of $H(t)$ as the energy by [F3], and the factor $f(t)Q$ carries the unit $\mathrm{J\,m^{-1}}\cdot\mathrm m=\mathrm J$ by [F3]. Applying clause (a) with $H(t)/\hbar$ gives the unique strong propagator with the strong equation on $D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ and domain invariance. This is clause (c).

[Scope] Only the common-domain class, the regularity $C^{1}(Y,H)$ and the oscillator's relative-boundedness structure were used; no explicit solution, no asymptotic, adiabatic or long-time statement, no measurement and no empirical comparison was formed, which is clause (d).
