Adopt the framework data and the **declared circular two-level drive model** of clause (f) of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]]: $\mathfrak H=\mathbb C^{2}$ with the orthonormal basis $(e_{\uparrow},e_{\downarrow})$ and the Pauli matrices $(\sigma_x,\sigma_y,\sigma_z)$ of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e), real parameters $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1},\omega$ and
$$H_{\mathrm c}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\Bigl(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\bigl(\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x}+\sin(\omega t)\sigma_{y}\bigr)\Bigr),\qquad t\in I=[t_{0},t_{1}],$$
read as the model's energy family in the bounded norm-continuous class, with $U_{\mathrm c}(t,s)$ its unique unitary propagator ([[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-bounded-norm-propagator]] clause (a)). Put $\Delta:=\omega_{0}-\omega$, $b:=\sqrt{\Delta^{2}+\Omega_{1}^{2}}$, let $R(t):=\cos(\omega t/2)I+i\sin(\omega t/2)\sigma_{z}$ be the rotating frame of [[lem-nrqm-driven-dynamics-two-level-rotating-frame]] and let $P_{\uparrow},P_{\downarrow}$ be the projections onto $\mathbb Ce_{\uparrow},\mathbb Ce_{\downarrow}$, with populations $p_{\bullet}(t):=\langle P_{\bullet}\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle$ of the evolved vector. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then (differential assertions apply when $t_0<t_1$, with one-sided endpoint derivatives; on a singleton the propagator identity and population formulas remain valid):

(a) *Exact rotating-frame reduction.* For every solution $\psi$ of $i\hbar\psi'(t)=H_{\mathrm c}(t)\psi(t)$ the rotating-frame vector $\psi_{R}(t):=R(t)\psi(t)$ satisfies exactly
$$i\hbar\psi_{R}'(t)=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\Delta\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\sigma_{x}\bigr)\psi_{R}(t),$$
with the constant matrix $\frac{\hbar}{2}(\Delta\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\sigma_{x})$; equivalently
$$U_{\mathrm c}(t,s)=R(t)^{*}\,e^{-i(t-s)(\Delta\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\sigma_{x})/2}\,R(s)\qquad(s,t\in I).$$

(b) *Rabi populations.* Let $\psi(s)=e_{\uparrow}$ at time $s$. Define $p_{\bullet}^{R}(\tau):=\langle P_{\bullet}\psi_R(s+\tau),\psi_R(s+\tau)\rangle$ for $\tau\in I-s:=\{t-s:t\in I\}$. Then for $\tau:=t-s$
$$p_{\downarrow}(t)=p_{\downarrow}^{R}(\tau)=\Bigl|\bigl\langle e_{\downarrow},e^{-i\tau(\Delta\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\sigma_{x})/2}e_{\uparrow}\bigr\rangle\Bigr|^{2}=\frac{\Omega_{1}^{2}}{b^{2}}\sin^{2}\!\Bigl(\frac{b\tau}{2}\Bigr)\qquad(b>0),$$
and $p_{\uparrow}(t)=1-p_{\downarrow}(t)$; the populations of the rotating-frame vector $\psi_{R}(t)$ are the same numbers.

(c) *Resonance and inversion times.* At resonance $\Delta=0$ one has $p_{\downarrow}(t)=\sin^{2}(\Omega_{1}\tau/2)$; when $\Omega_1\ne0$, the drive inverts the population fully at the **pi-pulse** time $\tau=\pi/|\Omega_{1}|$ and returns it to the initial level at $\tau=2\pi/|\Omega_{1}|$, whenever the respective evaluation time $s+\tau$ belongs to $I$; for $b>0$ the population obeys $p_{\downarrow}^{R}(\tau+2\pi/b)=p_{\downarrow}^{R}(\tau)$ whenever both elapsed times lie in $I-s$. For $\Omega_{1}=0$ the populations are constant, $p_{\downarrow}\equiv0$ and $p_{\uparrow}\equiv1$.

(d) *Scope.* The statements are exact for the declared finite model and its declared parameters; the rotating frame is a change of description of the same model and does not change the populations. The theorem asserts no damping or relaxation, no decoherence, no measurement record, no identification of $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1}$ with laboratory fields or of the two levels with a species, and no empirical value.

derivations.claim: [Resonant set] For every finite displayed evaluation choose a compact $J$ containing $s,t$; the all-real circular family is bounded and norm-continuous on $J$, so [L1] applies. Independence of $J$ follows from the norm Dyson uniqueness included in the model: restrictions from a larger interval solve the same initial integral equation on the smaller one. By [L1] with $\Delta=0$ one has $p_{\downarrow}=\sin^{2}(\Omega_{1}(t-s)/2)=\sin^{2}(t-s)$ because $\Omega_{1}=2$ by [L2]; at $t-s=\pi/4$ this is $\sin^{2}(\pi/4)=1/2$; at $t-s=\pi/2$ it is $\sin^{2}(\pi/2)=1$; and at $t-s=\pi$ it is $\sin^{2}(\pi)=0$, using $\sin(\pi/4)=\sqrt2/2$ and $\sin(\pi/2)=1$. This is clause (a).

[Detuned set] By [L1] and [L2], $p_{\downarrow}=\frac14\sin^{2}(t-s)$; at $t-s=\pi/2$ this is $\frac14\sin^{2}(\pi/2)=1/4$, and since $\sin^{2}$ has period $\pi$ the population is $\pi$-periodic in $t-s$. This is clause (b).

[Undriven set and reading] With $\Omega_{1}=0$ the family of clause (f) of the model is $\frac{\hbar\omega_{0}}{2}\sigma_{z}$, which is diagonal in the basis $(e_{\uparrow},e_{\downarrow})$, so $U_{\mathrm c}(t,s)=e^{-i\omega_{0}(t-s)\sigma_{z}/2}$ and $p_{\downarrow}\equiv0$, $p_{\uparrow}\equiv1$; writing $\sigma_{\pm}=\frac12(\sigma_{x}\pm i\sigma_{y})$ one has $e^{i\theta\sigma_{z}}\sigma_{\pm}e^{-i\theta\sigma_{z}}=e^{\pm 2i\theta}\sigma_{\pm}$ by the matrix products of clause (e), so $U_{\mathrm c}(t,s)^{*}\sigma_{\pm}U_{\mathrm c}(t,s)=e^{\pm i\omega_{0}(t-s)}\sigma_{\pm}$ so the phase identity holds for every initial vector, while for the specified up state the initial and evolved transverse coherences both vanish; in all three sets the numbers are outcome probabilities of the projection $P_{\downarrow}$ in the evolved preparation by the reading of clause (e) of the model, so no measurement or laboratory claim is made. These are clauses (c) and (d).

Adopt the framework data and the **declared linear two-level drive model** of clause (f) of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]]: $\mathfrak H=\mathbb C^{2}$, the orthonormal basis $(e_{\uparrow},e_{\downarrow})$ and Pauli matrices of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e), real parameters $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1},\omega$ with $\omega\ne0$, and
$$H_{\mathrm l}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x}\bigr),\qquad t\in I=[a,b],$$
read as the model's energy family in the bounded norm-continuous class with unique propagator $U_{\mathrm l}(t,s)$ ([[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-bounded-norm-propagator]] clause (a)). Put $\Delta:=\omega_{0}-\omega$, let $R(t):=\cos(\omega t/2)I+i\sin(\omega t/2)\sigma_{z}$ be the rotating frame of [[lem-nrqm-driven-dynamics-two-level-rotating-frame]], let $U_{\mathrm l}^{R}(t,s):=R(t)U_{\mathrm l}(t,s)R(s)^{*}$, and define the **averaged matrix** and the **counter-rotating amplitude**
$$A:=\frac{\hbar}{2}\Bigl(\Delta\sigma_{z}+\frac{\Omega_{1}}{2}\sigma_{x}\Bigr),\qquad B:=\frac{\hbar\Omega_{1}}{8}\bigl(\sigma_{x}+i\sigma_{y}\bigr),\qquad \varepsilon(\tau):=\frac{|\Omega_{1}|}{2|\omega|}\Bigl[1+\tau\Bigl(\frac{|\Delta|}{2}+\frac{3|\Omega_{1}|}{4}\Bigr)\Bigr].$$
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) *Exact rotating-frame family.* For every $t\in I$,
$$R(t)H_{\mathrm l}(t)R(t)^{*}+i\hbar R'(t)R(t)^{*}=A+e^{2i\omega t}B+e^{-2i\omega t}B^{*},$$
with $A=A^{*}$, $\|A/\hbar\|\le\frac12(|\Delta|+|\Omega_{1}|/2)$ and $\|B/\hbar\|=|\Omega_{1}|/4$; the second and third terms are the **counter-rotating terms** of the drive in the rotating frame.

(b) *Rotating-wave error contract.* For all $s,t\in I$, with $\tau:=|t-s|$,
$$\bigl\|U_{\mathrm l}^{R}(t,s)-e^{-i(t-s)A/\hbar}\bigr\|\le\varepsilon(\tau)=\frac{|\Omega_{1}|}{2|\omega|}\Bigl[1+\tau\Bigl(\frac{|\Delta|}{2}+\frac{3|\Omega_{1}|}{4}\Bigr)\Bigr];$$
the bound is uniform in $s$ for fixed $\tau$ and grows linearly in $\tau$.

(c) *Population comparison.* Let $\psi(s)=e_{\uparrow}$ and let $p_{\downarrow}(t):=\langle P_{\downarrow}\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle$ be the exact down-population at time $t$, where $\psi(t)=U_{\mathrm l}(t,s)e_{\uparrow}$. Let
$$p_{\downarrow}^{\mathrm{avg}}(\tau):=\frac{(\Omega_{1}/2)^{2}}{\Delta^{2}+(\Omega_{1}/2)^{2}}\,\sin^{2}\!\Bigl(\frac{\tau}{2}\sqrt{\Delta^{2}+\frac{\Omega_{1}^{2}}{4}}\Bigr)\qquad(\Omega_{1}\ne0),\qquad p_{\downarrow}^{\mathrm{avg}}\equiv0\quad(\Omega_{1}=0),$$
be the down-population of the initial up-state under the propagator of the **averaged family** $t\mapsto A$. Then for every $s,t\in I$
$$\bigl|p_{\downarrow}(t)-p_{\downarrow}^{\mathrm{avg}}(t-s)\bigr|\le 2\,\varepsilon(|t-s|).$$
At resonance $\Delta=0$ one has $p_{\downarrow}^{\mathrm{avg}}(\tau)=\sin^{2}(|\Omega_{1}|\tau/4)$.

- **(ii) Bounded-control class.** $H(t)=H_{0}+V(t)$, where $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(H_{0})\subseteq\mathfrak H$ and $V:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and $\|V(t)\|=v(t)$, $v:=\sup_{t\in I}v(t)<\infty$.
- **(iii) Common-domain class.** There is a dense linear subspace $Y\subseteq\mathfrak H$ that is itself a Hilbert space continuously embedded in $\mathfrak H$ ([[def-hilbert-space]], for instance $Y=D(H_{0})$ with the graph norm of a self-adjoint $H_{0}$), with $D(H(t))=Y$ for every $t$, each $H(t)$ self-adjoint as an operator on $\mathfrak H$, and $t\mapsto H(t)$ of class $C^{1}(I;\mathcal B(Y,\mathfrak H))$.

The family, its class and its data are **prescribed**: no field equation, source model, back-reaction or feedback of the system on the source is assumed, and no claim is made that any laboratory arrangement realizes the family. The family is coupled to the system through the material hypotheses of the page or of the item that declares a specific model (for instance a magnetic-moment or electric-dipole coupling, or the external-source Coulomb family of the page's adiabatic models); the reading of $H(t)$ as the energy of the declared system is a model assumption.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Adopt the
notation of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-driven-oscillator-common-domain]]:
$m,\omega,\hbar>0$, $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, $Q,P$ the position and
momentum operators, $H_{\mathrm{osc}}=\frac{P^2}{2m}+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}Q^2$ with
domain $Y=D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$, $f\in C^1([a,b];\mathbb R)$ and
$H(t)=H_{\mathrm{osc}}-f(t)Q$ self-adjoint on $Y$. For real $q,p$ define the
Weyl operator
$$D(q,p)\psi(x):=e^{ip(x-q/2)/\hbar}\,\psi(x-q).$$
For $s\le t$ in $[a,b]$ let $q(\cdot;s),p(\cdot;s)$ be the unique $C^1$ solution
of $q'=p/m$, $p'=-m\omega^2q+f$, $q(s)=p(s)=0$, and put
$S(t,s):=\int_s^tf(r)q(r)/2\,dr$. Then:

(a) $D(q,p)$ is unitary on $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$, preserves $Y$, and on $Y$ the
identities $D(q,p)^*QD(q,p)=Q+qI$, $D(q,p)^*PD(q,p)=P+pI$ hold; along a $C^1$
trajectory $t\mapsto(q(t),p(t))$ one has
$$i\hbar\,\partial_tD(q,p)\psi=\bigl[-p'Q+q'P+\tfrac12(qp'-pq')I\bigr]D(q,p)\psi\quad(\psi\in Y),$$
and the conjugation identity $H_{\mathrm{osc}}D=DH_{\mathrm{osc}}+\bigl[\frac pmP+m\omega^2qQ-\frac{p^2}{2m}-\frac{m\omega^2q^2}{2}\bigr]D$
holds on $Y$.

(b) The family
$$U(t,s):=e^{iS(t,s)/\hbar}D(q(t,s),p(t,s))e^{-i(t-s)H_{\mathrm{osc}}/\hbar}$$
is unitary, $U(s,s)=I$, preserves $Y$, satisfies the strong Schrödinger
equation $i\hbar\,\partial_tU(t,s)\psi=H(t)U(t,s)\psi$ for every $\psi\in Y$,
and provides the unique solution of that equation with $U(s,s)=I$; by density it
gives strongly continuous mild evolution on all of $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$, with
the cocycle property on $[a,b]$.

(c) *Coherent-state check.* Define the coherent vector in the scaled Hermite basis by $\psi_z:=e^{-|z|^2/2}\sum_{n\ge0}z^n\psi_n/\sqrt{n!}$ for $z\in\mathbb C$ (the series converges in $L^2$). If $f\equiv0$, then
$U(t,s)\psi_z=e^{-i\omega(t-s)/2}\psi_{ze^{-i\omega(t-s)}}$, recovering the
undriven dynamics.

No statement about arbitrary unbounded potentials or varying domains is made.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$m,\omega,\hbar>0$, let $\ell:=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, let
$H_{\mathrm{osc}}=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}DAD^{-1}$ be the oscillator of
[[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] with
orthonormal eigenbasis $(\psi_n)_{n\ge0}$ and ladder operators
$a_\psi,a_\psi^\dagger,N_\psi$ of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]]
transported to $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$. Work with $\langle u,v\rangle=\int u\overline v$, linear in its first argument, and define $N_\psi^{1/2}$ by the coefficient action $\sqrt n\,c_n$ on $D(N_\psi^{1/2})=\{\psi:\sum_n n|c_n|^2<\infty\}$, where $c_n=\langle\psi,\psi_n\rangle$. Use the negative-sign $2\pi$ Fourier convention $\widehat u(\xi)=\int e^{-2\pi i x\xi}u(x)\,dx$ on integrable inputs and its Plancherel extension $\mathcal F_2$. Let
$Q=M_x$, $P=\mathcal F_2^*M_{2\pi\hbar\xi}\mathcal F_2$ be the maximal
position and momentum operators (their self-adjointness is proved below), with
$D(Q)=\{\psi:x\psi\in L^2\}$ and
$D(P)=\{\psi:\xi\mathcal F_2\psi\in L^2\}$, with
$H_{\mathrm{osc}}=\hbar\omega(N_\psi+\frac12I)$ and the couplings
$$Q=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}(a_\psi+a_\psi^\dagger),\qquad P=\frac{\hbar}{i\ell\sqrt2}(a_\psi-a_\psi^\dagger)$$
on the common domain $D(N_\psi^{1/2})$. Let $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ be of class
$C^1$. Put $Y:=D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})=D(N_\psi)$ with graph norm
$\|\psi\|_Y^2:=\|\psi\|^2+\|H_{\mathrm{osc}}\psi\|^2$. Then:

(a) *Ladder bounds.* For every $\psi\in D(N_\psi^{1/2})$,
$$\|Q\psi\|\le\ell\bigl(2\|N_\psi^{1/2}\psi\|^2+\|\psi\|^2\bigr)^{1/2},\qquad \|P\psi\|\le\frac{\hbar}{\ell}\bigl(2\|N_\psi^{1/2}\psi\|^2+\|\psi\|^2\bigr)^{1/2}.$$

(b) *Infinitesimal bound.* For every $\eta>0$ there is $b_\eta<\infty$ with
$\|Q\psi\|\le\eta\|H_{\mathrm{osc}}\psi\|+b_\eta\|\psi\|$ for
$\psi\in Y=D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$; hence $-f(t)Q$ is
$H_{\mathrm{osc}}$-bounded with relative bound $0$ for every fixed $t$
([[def-relative-boundedness-with-respect-to-an-operator]]).

(c) *Common domain.* For every $t\in[a,b]$ the operator
$H(t):=H_{\mathrm{osc}}-f(t)Q$ is self-adjoint on the single domain $Y$
(independent of $t$); moreover $t\mapsto H(t)$ belongs to
$C^1([a,b];\mathcal B(Y,L^2))$ with derivative $-f'(t)Q$, so the family has a
common domain and satisfies the regularity hypothesis of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-common-domain-nonautonomous-evolution]].

Adopt the framework data and the declared driven model of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] in the **common-domain class** of clause (b)(iii): $\mathfrak H$ is the model's state space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), $Y\subseteq\mathfrak H$ is a dense linear subspace that is itself a Hilbert space continuously embedded in $\mathfrak H$, $D(H(t))=Y$ for every $t\in I=[a,b]$, every $H(t)$ is self-adjoint as an operator on $\mathfrak H$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), and $t\mapsto H(t)$ is of class $C^{1}(I;\mathcal B(Y,\mathfrak H))$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]); put $A(t):=H(t)/\hbar$ and, when $a<b$, $L:=\sup_{t\in I}\|H'(t)\|_{\mathcal B(Y,\mathfrak H)}<\infty$; for $a=b$ set $L:=0$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then (all differential assertions below apply only when $a<b$, with one-sided derivatives at endpoints; for $a=b$ only $U(a,a)=I$ and the domain, norm and algebraic assertions are claimed):

(a) *Well-posedness of the declared model.* There is a family $U(t,s)$, $a\le s\le t\le b$ on $I$, of unitary operators on $\mathfrak H$ with $U(s,s)=I$, the cocycle $U(t,r)=U(t,s)U(s,r)$, joint strong continuity in $(t,s)$, and:
$$U(t,s)Y=Y,\qquad \|U(t,s)y\|_Y\le C_{I}\|y\|_Y\quad(y\in Y), \qquad i\hbar\,\partial_{t}U(t,s)y=H(t)U(t,s)y\quad(y\in Y),$$
where the derivative is in $\mathfrak H$ and $C_{I}<\infty$ is independent of the endpoints and depends on the actual graph equivalence of $Y$ with $D(H(t)/\hbar)$ as well as $I$ and $L/\hbar$; this family is unique among bounded families with the same strong equation on $Y$, $U(s,s)=I$ and locally bounded strong orbits. The model's clause (c)(iii) declaration therefore has exactly one solution.

(b) *Reverse and adjoint equations.* With $U(s,t):=U(t,s)^{-1}$ one has $U(t,s)^{*}=U(s,t)$ and $i\hbar\partial_{s}U(t,s)y=-U(t,s)H(s)y$ for $y\in Y$; equivalently $i\hbar\partial_{s}U(s,t)y=H(s)U(s,t)y$. The domain maps $(t,s)\mapsto U(t,s)|_{Y}$ are jointly strongly continuous in $\mathcal B(Y)$.

(c) *Declared instance: the driven oscillator.* Let $m,\omega,\hbar>0$ and let $(H_{\mathrm{osc}},Q)$ be the energy and position observables of the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (b), (c) on $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$, with $Y=D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ carrying the graph norm, and let $f\in C^{1}(I;\mathbb R)$. Declare, as a further model assumption of the pair, the **driven oscillator family**
$$H(t):=H_{\mathrm{osc}}-f(t)Q\qquad(t\in I),$$
read as the system's energy at time $t$, with $f(t)Q$ in joules for $f(t)$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-1}}$. Then for every $t$ the operator $H(t)$ is self-adjoint on the single domain $Y$, the family belongs to $C^{1}(I;\mathcal B(Y,L^{2}))$ with derivative $-f'(t)Q$, and the hypotheses of clause (a) are satisfied with $\mathfrak H=L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$; consequently the driven oscillator has a unique strong propagator preserving $D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ and satisfying $i\hbar\partial_{t}U(t,s)y=H(t)U(t,s)y$ for $y\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$.

(d) *Scope.* The theorem is conditional on the common-domain regularity class and on the cited oscillator construction; it asserts no existence statement outside that class, no explicit solution, no long-time or adiabatic statement, no measurement and no empirical comparison.

**(a) Setting.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 in the reading of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]) and the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (a), (b), (c), with parameters $m>0$, $\omega>0$, action constant $\hbar>0$ and length scale $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(g_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be the Hermite family of $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$, let $D:L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)\to L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$ be the scaling unitary and $(\psi_n)$ the scaled eigenbasis of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (a), (b), with $\psi_n=Dg_n$; let $a_\psi=DaD^{-1}$ be the transported annihilation operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]], and let $N_\psi=DND^{-1}$ be the model's assigned excitation-number observable of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clause (c), with its stated domain and unit $1$.

**(b) The family.** For $z\in\mathbb C$ let $\psi^{(y)}_z$ be the coherent vector of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-convergence]] clause (a),
$$\psi^{(y)}_z:=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}\,g_n\in L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy),$$
the series converging in $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$, and define the model's **coherent state** with label $z$ by
$$\Psi_z:=D\psi^{(y)}_z=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}\,\psi_n\in\mathcal H_1 .$$
The family $(\Psi_z)_{z\in\mathbb C}$ is the model's **coherent-state family**, and $z$ is its **amplitude-phase label**.

**(c) Basic properties.** The following properties of the family are those established in the cited items and are recorded here as part of the definition's reading: the series for $\Psi_z$ converges and $\|\Psi_z\|=1$, so by P1 the ray $[\Psi_z]$ is a pure preparation of the model when it is declared as one; $\Psi_z\in D(N_\psi^{k})$ for every $k\in\mathbb N$; $a_\psi\Psi_z=z\Psi_z$, so $\Psi_z$ is a unit eigenvector of the annihilation operator with eigenvalue $z$; $\langle\Psi_z,\Psi_w\rangle=e^{-(|z|^{2}+|w|^{2})/2+z\overline w}$, with modulus $e^{-|z-w|^{2}/2}$ for all $z,w$, so distinct labels define distinct preparations (their overlap modulus is less than $1$, whereas unit vectors on the same ray have overlap modulus $1$) and no two members of the family are orthogonal; and $\Psi_0=\psi_0$ is the ground eigenvector of the energy operator. ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-convergence]] clauses (a), (b), (c), (d), (e), transported by the unitary $D$ of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clause (a).)

**(d) Reading of the label.** The label $z$ is dimensionless (it is a complex number, not a quantity with a physical dimension). Its amplitude is $|z|$; when $z\ne0$, its phase is the class $\arg z\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, while $z=0$ has zero amplitude and no phase label. The mathematical coherent-state series gives the quadratic-form value $\langle N_\psi\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=|z|^{2}$ for the assigned, dimensionless excitation-number observable $(N_\psi,1)$; this is the number coordinate intended by the model's P2 reading. Under the model's flow, [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-evolution-and-variance]] clauses (c), (e), (f) gives $U(t)\Psi_z=e^{-i\omega t/2}\Psi_{ze^{-i\omega t}}$ and the position and momentum means $\sqrt2\ell\operatorname{Re}(ze^{-i\omega t})$ and $\sqrt2\hbar\operatorname{Im}(ze^{-i\omega t})/\ell$, respectively; thus the mean pair, in coordinates scaled by $\sqrt2\ell$ and $\sqrt2\hbar/\ell$, rotates with the phase label at angular frequency $\omega$. Clause (d) records this interpretation of the label, not an outcome of measuring the label itself.

**(e) Scope.** The definition declares a one-parameter family of preparations of the one-dimensional model and fixes its notation. It does not assert that the coherent states are the only preparations with time-independent position or momentum spreads, it does not assert minimality of any uncertainty product (that is a separate result for this family), it does not construct a displacement operator, an overcompleteness relation or a resolution of unity, and it makes no measurement, apparatus or empirical claim. The two presentations of the family -- as eigenvectors of the annihilation operator, as in clause (b), and as translated ground states -- are not identified here; only the former is defined.

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (a), (b), (c), and the coherent-state family of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-states]]; assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $U(t)=\exp(-itH_1/\hbar)$ be the model's flow, let $\Psi_z$ be the coherent state of label $z\in\mathbb C$, put $z(t):=ze^{-i\omega t}$, and define $x_0:=\sqrt2\,\ell\operatorname{Re}z$, $p_0:=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z$ for every $z\in\mathbb C$. Then:

(a) **Coherent evolution.** For every $t\in\mathbb R$, $U(t)$ is a bijective linear isometry of $\mathcal H_1$ and
$$U(t)\Psi_z=e^{-i\omega t/2}\,\Psi_{z(t)};$$
consequently the preparation $[\Psi_z]$ evolves under the model's Schroedinger dynamics to the coherent preparation $[\Psi_{z(t)}]$, and the labels of the evolved family rotate with angular frequency $\omega$;

(b) **Classical mean motion.** The preparation means of position and momentum at time $t$ are
$$\langle Q\rangle_{z(t)}=\sqrt2\,\ell\operatorname{Re}z(t),\qquad \langle P\rangle_{z(t)}=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z(t),$$
equivalently, for every $t\in\mathbb R$, $x(t)=x_0\cos\omega t+\frac{p_0}{m\omega}\sin\omega t$ and $p(t)=p_0\cos\omega t-m\omega x_0\sin\omega t$ with $x(t):=\langle Q\rangle_{z(t)}$, $p(t):=\langle P\rangle_{z(t)}$; these functions are differentiable with $\dot x(t)=\frac{p(t)}{m}$ and $\dot p(t)=-m\omega^{2}x(t)$ for every $t$, so the means follow the classical harmonic motion of frequency $\omega$ through $(x_0,p_0)$;

(c) **Stationary fluctuations.** For every $t\in\mathbb R$ the evolved preparation has
$$\Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}Q=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}P=\frac{\hbar}{\ell\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}Q\,\Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}P=\frac{\hbar}{2};$$
the position and momentum spreads and their product are constant along the evolution;

(d) **Energy statistics.** The mean and the outcome law of the assigned energy observable in the coherent preparation are
$$\langle H_1\rangle_{z}=\hbar\omega\Bigl(|z|^{2}+\frac12\Bigr),\qquad \mu^{H_1}_{\Psi_z}\bigl(\{\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)\}\bigr)=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}\quad(n\in\mathbb N),$$
the pushforward under $n\mapsto\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)$ of the **Poisson law** on $\mathbb N$ with parameter $s:=|z|^2$, defined by the weights $p_n=e^{-s}s^n/n!$, with $s^0=1$ also at $s=0$; consequently $\Delta_{\Psi_z}H_1=\hbar\omega|z|$;

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P4, P5, the adopted oscillator model, the model's spectrum theorem, the coherent-state fluctuation theorem and the cited mathematics. They concern the exact evolution of the model's coherent preparations and the statistics of its assigned observables; no measurement record, no apparatus realization, no damping or driving and no empirical value is asserted, and the identification of the mean motion with the motion of a laboratory oscillator is a tested identification under P7.

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (a), (b), (c), and the coherent-state family of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-states]]; assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $Q$ and $P$ be the model's position and momentum observables with their declared units ($\mathrm m$ and $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$), let $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, let $\Delta_{\rho}A$ be the preparation spread of an assigned sharp observable in the reading of [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]], and write $\langle A\rangle_z:=\langle A\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle$ for the model's coherent preparation of label $z$. Then:

(a) **Coherent spreads.** For every $z\in\mathbb C$ the vector $\Psi_z$ lies in $D(Q)\cap D(P)$, the preparation spreads of $Q$ and $P$ in the pure preparation of $\Psi_z$ exist, and
$$\Delta_{\Psi_z}Q=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\frac{\hbar}{\ell\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_z}Q\,\Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\frac{\hbar}{2};$$

(b) **Position-momentum relation of the model.** Every unit vector $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$ satisfies
$$\Delta_{f}Q\,\Delta_{f}P\ge\frac{\hbar}{2},$$
read in the product unit $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{2}\mathrm s^{-1}$; consequently the value $\hbar/2$ attained in (a) is the minimum over the common domain, and it is attained by every coherent preparation;

(c) **Saturation.** For every $z\in\mathbb C$, with the centered vectors
$$x_z:=(Q-\langle Q\rangle_zI)\Psi_z,\qquad y_z:=(P-\langle P\rangle_zI)\Psi_z,$$
one has $\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=-i\hbar/2$; in particular $\operatorname{Re}\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=0$ and $x_z,y_z$ are linearly dependent, so $\|x_z\|\,\|y_z\|=|\langle x_z,y_z\rangle|=\hbar/2$;

(d) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P5, the adopted oscillator model, the cited preparation-moment and uncertainty results and the cited mathematics. They concern the spreads of the two separately assigned outcome laws of $Q$ and $P$ in one preparation; they introduce no joint outcome law of position and momentum, no measurement error, no disturbance of the preparation, no dynamics and no empirical value. Whether a laboratory preparation and apparatus realize the pair of observables and produce this spread is a tested identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$. If $A$ has no eigenvalues, every preparation has an atomless outcome law: each singleton has probability zero, while $\mathbb R$ remains the outcome space and the law is concentrated on $\sigma(A)$ as in clause (d). Zero singleton probability does not exclude real point values as realizations of this law; it supplies no normalized exact-value eigenstate. A finite-resolution record is read through its declared Borel bin, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

**Density operators.** Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space. A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a) ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). The **state space** of $H$ is the set of all density operators on $H$ and is denoted
$$D(H):=\{\rho:\rho\ \text{is a density operator on}\ H\}.$$
An element of $D(H)$ is called a **state** of $H$ in the mathematical sense fixed here.

**Pure states.** A state $\rho\in D(H)$ is **pure** when there is a unit vector $u\in S(H)$ with
$$\rho=T_{u,u},\qquad T_{u,u}x=\langle x,u\rangle u\quad(x\in H),$$
where $T_{u,u}$ is the rank-one operator of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] and $S(H)$ is the unit sphere of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. By [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] the pure states are exactly the Hilbert orthogonal projections of $H$ with one-dimensional range, and the map
$$j:R(H)\longrightarrow D(H),\qquad j([\psi]):=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)},$$
on the ray space $R(H)$, with $\nu$ the normalization map, is well defined and injective with image the set of pure states. A state is **mixed** when it is not pure. For a nonzero vector $\psi$ the **normalized rank-one operator of $\psi$** is
$$\widehat\rho(\psi):=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\operatorname{tr}(T_{\psi,\psi})},$$
which equals $T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)}$; thus $\widehat\rho(\psi)$ is the pure state of the ray $[\psi]$, and the vector $\psi$ enters only through its ray.

**Purity.** For $\rho\in D(H)$ the operator $\rho^{2}$ is self-adjoint, positive and trace class: it is self-adjoint by the adjoint algebra of [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]], positive because $\langle\rho^{2}x,x\rangle=\langle\rho x,\rho x\rangle\ge0$, and trace class because $\rho$ is a bounded trace-class operator and the trace-class operators form a two-sided ideal ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]] clauses 1 and 2). The **purity** of $\rho$ is the real number
$$\mathcal P(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{2})\in\mathbb R.$$
The numerical range of the purity and the equivalence of purity with purity of the state are established by the purity criterion of this page; this definition records the object only.

**Scope.** This definition fixes the mathematical state space of a Hilbert space together with the pure states, the mixed states, the normalized rank-one operator of a nonzero vector and the purity functional. The cited rank-one calculus and the density-operator expansion assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), and the definition is read under that assumption. It asserts no dynamics, no measurement, no probability law and no physical interpretation, and it introduces no new assumptions beyond the cited mathematics and that choice hypothesis. In particular, whether a given physical preparation is described by a pure or a mixed state is a question about the model's assignments, not about this definition.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework, for systems in the declared massive-matter sector, the following statements about states and their composition. Assume throughout the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), which is the choice hypothesis of the mathematical suppliers cited below.

**(i) State space.** To each physical system of the sector the model assigns a complex Hilbert space $H$ that is nonzero and separable: a complex Hilbert space in the sense of [[def-hilbert-space]] which admits a sequence whose range is dense in $H$, so that the hypothesis of [[thm-separable-hilbert-space-has-a-countable-orthonormal-basis]] holds and $H$ has a finite or countable orthonormal basis. The assignment of a Hilbert space to a physical system is a model assumption; the linear structure used to combine descriptions mathematically is not an empirical claim. The physical system to which $H$ is assigned, and the sector in which the assignment is made, are declared with it.

**(ii) Pure preparations.** A **pure preparation** of the system is a unit ray $[\psi]=\{z\psi:z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\}$ of a vector $\psi\in H$ with $\|\psi\|=1$; that is, two nonzero vectors describe the same pure preparation exactly when they differ by a nonzero complex factor. The zero vector is not a state and no preparation is assigned to it: the normalization $\|\psi\|=1$ is part of the assignment. The ray allows arbitrary nonzero rescaling; between unit representatives the factor has modulus one and is a **global phase**, which has no observable consequence (P2). The rank-one operator $T_{\psi,\psi}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] is the density operator associated with the ray of $\psi$.

**(iii) General preparations and mixing.** A general preparation of the system is a **density operator**: a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ on $H$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)). Pure preparations are the special case $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ with $\|\psi\|=1$. A **statistical mixture** of preparations $\rho_{n}$ with weights $w_{n}\ge0$, $\sum_{n}w_{n}=1$, is the trace-norm convergent sum $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}$ as follows directly in the trace-class Banach space ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]): each density has trace norm one, so $\sum_n\|w_n\rho_n\|_1=1$ gives trace-norm convergence. Every partial sum is positive; operator-norm convergence preserves its nonnegative quadratic forms, and continuity of trace gives $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). Thus the limit is again a density operator, without requiring the components to be orthogonal pure states. The weights are a classical preparation uncertainty and are not amplitudes. Distinct weighted ensembles of pure states may define the same $\rho$.

**(iv) Composition.** Two independent distinguishable subsystems with state spaces $H_{A}$ and $H_{B}$ are composed by the completed Hilbert tensor product $H_{A}\widehat\otimes H_{B}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. Product preparations $\psi_{A}\otimes\psi_{B}$ are simple tensors and are the special case in which each subsystem has its own specified preparation. Their finite linear span is dense in $H_{A}\widehat\otimes H_{B}$ by the construction; a pure composite preparation may be any unit ray in this completion, including a norm limit of finite linear combinations of product vectors, and need not factor. General composite preparations are density operators on this space and include the statistical mixtures of clause (iii). A quantity of subsystem $A$ alone is represented on the composite by an operator of the form $A\otimes I_{B}$ and a quantity of $B$ alone by $I_{A}\otimes B$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] (bounded case; unbounded local operators are treated where they occur). The existence of the completed tensor product is mathematics; the assignment of that product to a composite physical system is the physical assumption here.

**(v) Restrictions that are separate assumptions.** Restrictions of the state space by superselection rules, identical-particle symmetry sectors, and the replacement of the tensor product by more general algebraic structures are not consequences of the clauses above: where such a restriction is used it is adopted separately, and the identical-species sectors are the subject of the postulate P6 of this page.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model within its declared sector. They are not derived from experiment, and they do not assert that a physical system is exactly described by such a Hilbert space; no numerical measurement is recorded. The compatibility of the framework with observation is a question about fully specified models and reported data, in the sense of P7.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following statements about sharp and unsharp real-valued quantities. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The latter is the explicit hypothesis used to obtain the spectral PVM of a general self-adjoint operator from [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] in clause (ii); consumers invoking this construction inherit it.

**(i) Sharp observables.** An **ideal sharp real-valued quantity** (observable) of a system with state space $H$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), meaning $D(A)=D(A^*)$ and $A\psi=A^*\psi$ on this common domain, together with a declared unit in which its real spectral coordinate is read; the unit is part of the assignment, and no numerical value of the coordinate is asserted by the assignment. Symmetry of $A$ on a small domain is not sufficient for self-adjointness, and the domain is a declared part of the observable.

**(ii) Spectral probability.** Let $E_{A}$ be the spectral projection-valued measure of the self-adjoint operator $A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$ and a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ the **probability of the outcome in $B$** is
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_{A}(B)\bigr),\qquad\text{and for a pure preparation }[\psi]\text{ it is }\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}.$$
By clause (b) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] the assignment $B\mapsto\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$ is a probability measure on the Borel sets ([[def-probability-measure]], [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). It is the general form of the Born rule adopted here.

**(iii) Nature of the outcome law.** The probability law is a measure, not necessarily a density with respect to Lebesgue measure and not necessarily a finite or countable sum of point masses: a self-adjoint operator with continuous spectrum ordinarily has no normalizable eigenvector at a point of its continuous spectrum, so an "exact value" of a continuum quantity is not represented by a normalized state. An ideal point value is an idealization; a real detector reports a finite-resolution outcome, that is, the probability of a declared Borel set $B$ such as a bin, and the recorded-event probability is that of (ii) for the bin, not the value of a density at a point.

**(iv) Unsharp finite outcomes.** Outcomes of a finite-resolution apparatus with finitely many channels are described, when the idealization uses bounded effects, by a finite family $(F_{a})_{a=1}^{p}$ of effects on $H$ as defined above, with $\sum_aF_a=I$. The **outcome probabilities** are $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$. They are normalized for every state space assigned by P1, as shown by the preceding general-$H$ calculation. This unsharp extension is an operational description tied to an apparatus model; it is not obtained from the sharp observable by mathematical manipulation alone, and the effects alone do not determine what happens to the state after the outcome (P3).

**(v) Moments are a separate matter.** Statements about the mean, variance or higher moments of the outcome law require the corresponding integrability of $t\mapsto t^{n}$ against $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ and are not part of this postulate; where they are used they are stated with their hypotheses. In particular the existence of $\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$ for an unbounded $A$ is not asserted.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model. They assert nothing about which quantities of a concrete apparatus are sharp, about the physical mechanism producing an outcome or about the completeness of the description; a laboratory record is a classical event whose relation to the model is a tested identification with uncertainty, in the sense of P7.

**(a) Dimensions.** Write $\ell$, $\tau$, $\mu$, $\vartheta$ for the four independent dimension symbols of length, duration, mass and electric charge. A **dimension** is an element of $\mathbb Q^{4}$, written $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ with $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb Q$; products and inverses of dimensions are componentwise addition and negation, and the dimensionless dimension $\ell^{0}\tau^{0}\mu^{0}\vartheta^{0}$ is abbreviated $1$. The conventions assign to each quantity of the framework a dimension $[X]$, subject to $[XY]=[X][Y]$, $[X/Y]=[X][Y]^{-1}$ and $[dX/du]=[X][u]^{-1}$, with sums meaningful only between quantities of equal dimension, in which case the sum carries that dimension. For a rational power $q$, dimension powers mean $[X]^q=\ell^{qa}\tau^{qb}\mu^{qc}\vartheta^{qd}$ when $[X]=\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$. Rational exponents include the half-integer wave-function dimensions in clause (d); the integer-exponent dimensions form the subgroup $\mathbb Z^4$. These are consistency requirements on the conventions, not laws of nature.

For extensions using temperature, adjoin an independent dimension symbol $\Theta$: the enlarged group is $\mathbb Q^4\times\mathbb Q$, written $\ell^a\tau^b\mu^c\vartheta^d\Theta^e$, with the same componentwise rules. The preceding group embeds by $e=0$, so all previously assigned dimensions are preserved. Temperature has dimension $\Theta$, the Boltzmann constant has dimension $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-2}\Theta^{-1}$, and entropy in joules per kelvin has that same dimension; a dimensionless entropy remains dimensionless. This convention does not assign a temperature or an entropy to any system.

**(b) Reference units.** The **metre** (m), **second** (s), **kilogram** (kg) and **coulomb** (C) are the reference units of length, duration, mass and charge; a quantity of dimension $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ is expressed in the unit $\mathrm m^{a}\mathrm s^{b}\mathrm kg^{c}\mathrm C^{d}$. Coordinates of an inertial frame are read with the time coordinate $t$ in seconds, $[t]=\tau$, and the spatial coordinates $x_{i}$ in metres, $[x_{i}]=\ell$; slice distances of the arena are read in metres. In the temperature extension the reference unit of $\Theta$ is the kelvin (K), so the general reference unit gains a factor $\mathrm K^e$.

**(c) Defining constants of the current SI.** The framework keeps $\hbar$ explicit. In the current SI the constants $h$, $c$ and $e$ are exact defining constants, with the values $h=6{,}626\,070\,15\times10^{-34}$ J s, $c=2{,}99792458\times10^{8}$ m s$^{-1}$ and $e=1{,}602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}$ C, and $\hbar:=h/(2\pi)$. These are real scalar constants with dimensions and units $[h]=[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$ (J s), $[c]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ (m s$^{-1}$), and $[e]=\vartheta$ (C). The vacuum permeability $\mu_{0}$ is a positive real scalar that is experimentally determined in the current SI, with $[\mu_{0}]=\mu\ell\vartheta^{-2}$ (N A$^{-2}$ = H m$^{-1}$); $\varepsilon_{0}:=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1}$ is a positive real scalar with $[\varepsilon_{0}]=\mu^{-1}\ell^{-3}\tau^{2}\vartheta^{2}$ (F m$^{-1}$). These are unit-convention statements of the SI, not measurements reported by this framework; $c$ enters the framework only through the separate radiation assumptions adopted on their own pages, not in the nonrelativistic spacetime of [[def-nrqm-framework-newtonian-spacetime]].

**(d) Dimensions and types of the framework's quantities.** The dimension map is fixed on the following quantities.

1. State quantities: a position wave function of a system with $d$ spatial dimensions and $r$ internal components is an almost-everywhere equivalence class in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with dimension $\ell^{-d/2}$, its norm $\|\psi\|$ is dimensionless, and an abstract normalized state and the density operators of the state postulate are dimensionless.
2. Probability: the outcome probability $\mu(B)$ of the observable postulate is a dimensionless number; a position density $|\psi|^{2}$ has dimension $\ell^{-d}$; a momentum wave function normalized against $\mathrm d^{d}p$ has dimension $(\mu\ell\tau^{-1})^{-d/2}$; an amplitude for a finite outcome is a dimensionless complex number, while an amplitude read against a detector coordinate carries the square-root of the inverse of the detector measure.
3. Frame parameters ([[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]]): $[b]=\tau$, $[a_{i}]=\ell$, $[v_{i}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ and $[R_{ij}]=1$.
4. Mechanical quantities: action $[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; energy and the Hamiltonian eigenvalues $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$; momentum $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$; position components $\ell$; angular momentum and spin $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; mass $\mu$; velocity of a free spinless model $\ell\tau^{-1}$; force $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$; a real potential energy $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$.
5. Probability current: in the ordinary continuous-field regime, fix an integer $d\ge1$, an open spatial region $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ and an open time interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$. A **probability current density** is a declared continuous map $j:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^d$, whose spatial components have dimension $\ell^{1-d}\tau^{-1}$ and reference unit $\mathrm m^{1-d}\mathrm s^{-1}$. At fixed time it is a spatial vector field; its signed normal component is read as probability transported per unit spatial $(d-1)$-area and time. Explicitly, for a flat face $S=\{x:x_k=a,\ a_i\le x_i\le b_i\ (i\ne k)\}\subset\Omega$, with $a_i<b_i$ and chosen normal $n=\epsilon e_k$, $\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}$, define its **signed probability flux** at $t\in I$ as $\Phi_S(t):=\epsilon\int_{\prod_{i\ne k}[a_i,b_i]}j_k(x_1,\ldots,x_{k-1},a,x_{k+1},\ldots,x_d,t)\prod_{i\ne k}dx_i$. Here $e_k$ is the $k$th coordinate unit vector and the integral uses $(d-1)$-dimensional Lebesgue measure; for $d=1$ this means $\Phi_{\{a\}}(t)=\epsilon j(a,t)$. The flux has dimension $\tau^{-1}$ and unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$; positive sign means transport in the chosen normal direction. Fluxes through curved surfaces, or currents with weaker regularity, require separately specified surface measures or traces. This fixes the quantity type and flux convention; it supplies neither a current associated to an arbitrary $L^2$ state nor a conservation or detector law. Each dynamical model supplies its current construction and balance hypotheses.
6. Electric quantities of the model parameters: charge has dimension $\vartheta$; a magnetic moment has dimension $\ell^{2}\vartheta\tau^{-1}$, equivalently $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{2}=\mathrm J\,\mathrm T^{-1}$, and a gyromagnetic parameter $\gamma$ in the relation $\boldsymbol\mu=\gamma\mathbf S$ has dimension $\mu^{-1}\vartheta$, equivalently $\mathrm s^{-1}\mathrm T^{-1}$; these quantities appear only in the model assumptions that introduce them.
7. Statistical quantities: a mean has the dimension of its outcome coordinate, a variance the square of it and a standard deviation it; a mean, variance or higher moment exists only when the corresponding moment of the outcome probability is finite, so a symbolic average is not a number unless that integrability is established. Angles and phases are dimensionless under the radian convention.
8. Quantities of later extension assumptions - radiation frequencies and energies, electric dipole moments, cross sections, temperatures and entropies - are declared with their dimensions and units by the items that introduce those assumptions, under the rules fixed here; they are not part of the present list.

**(e) Conventions only.** No numerical value of any model parameter is fixed by this item: no mass, charge, spin label, potential or measured constant is asserted, and natural-unit shorthand (for example setting $\hbar=1$ or $c=1$) is read as an abbreviation for the corresponding SI-dimensioned statement with the constant restored.

derivations.claim: [Free coherent rotation] By [L2] with $\tau=t-s$ and $w=z$: $\Phi:=e^{-i\tau H_{\mathrm{osc}}/\hbar}\Psi_{z}=e^{-i\omega\tau/2}\Psi_{z(\tau)}$ with $z(\tau)=ze^{-i\omega\tau}$; hence $\langle Q\Phi,\Phi\rangle=\sqrt2\ell\operatorname{Re}z(\tau)$ and $\langle P\Phi,\Phi\rangle=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z(\tau)$, while $\|(Q-\langle Q\rangle I)\Phi\|^{2}=\ell^{2}/2$ and $\|(P-\langle P\rangle I)\Phi\|^{2}=\hbar^{2}/(2\ell^{2})$.

[Displacement shifts the means, not the spreads] Let $\Phi\in Y$ be unit and let $q,p\in\mathbb R$; $D:=D(q,p)$ is unitary and preserves $Y$, and $D^{*}QD=Q+qI$, $D^{*}PD=P+pI$ on $Y$ by [L1], so $$\langle QD\Phi,D\Phi\rangle=\langle D^{*}QD\Phi,\Phi\rangle=\langle Q\Phi,\Phi\rangle+q,\qquad \langle PD\Phi,D\Phi\rangle=\langle P\Phi,\Phi\rangle+p,$$ and unitarity gives $\|QD\Phi-\langle QD\Phi,D\Phi\rangle D\Phi\|=\|(Q-\langle Q\Phi,\Phi\rangle I)\Phi\|$, so the spreads of $D\Phi$ equal those of $\Phi$.

[Both time orientations] For all $s,t\in[a,b]$ use oriented integrals $q(t;s)=(m\omega)^{-1}\int_s^t\sin(\omega(t-r))f(r)\,dr$ and $p(t;s)=\int_s^t\cos(\omega(t-r))f(r)\,dr$, where $\int_s^t=-\int_t^s$ for $t<s$. Differentiating gives the declared equations and zero data in either direction; the energy $p^2/(2m)+m\omega^2q^2/2$ of the difference of two solutions is constant and initially zero, proving uniqueness. Set $S(t,s)=\int_s^t f(r)q(r;s)/2\,dr$ and $W(t,s)=e^{iS(t,s)/\hbar}D(q(t;s),p(t;s))e^{-i(t-s)H_{\mathrm{osc}}/\hbar}$. The displacement identities of [L1] apply along every real $C^1$ trajectory, and the free group preserves $Y$; their product derivative on each $y\in Y$ is justified by expanding $D(t+h)F(t+h)y-D(t)F(t)y$ as $D(t+h)(F(t+h)-F(t))y+(D(t+h)-D(t))F(t)y$, using strong continuity and unit norm of $D$ and the fixed vector $F(t)y\in Y$. Writing $E=p^2/(2m)+m\omega^2q^2/2$, [L1] gives $i\hbar\partial_t W=[H_{\mathrm{osc}}+(-p'-m\omega^2q)Q+(q'-p/m)P+(E+(qp'-pq')/2-S')I]W$. The differential equations give the $Q,P$ coefficients $-f,0$ and $E+(qp'-pq')/2=fq/2=S'$, so $W$ solves the strong equation with $W(s,s)=I$ on either side of $s$. The common-domain uniqueness in [L1] (or the constant-norm difference argument) identifies $W=U$ on $Y$, then on $L^2$ by density and unitarity. This is also the oriented extension proved in [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-explicit-unbounded-oscillator-propagator]] Proof, the paragraph beginning “Let $v(t)$ and $w(t)$ be two $Y$-valued strong solutions”. For $a=b$, all integrals vanish and $W(a,a)=I$ directly.

[Total response] By step 1.3, $U(t,s)\Psi_{z}=e^{iS/\hbar}D(q(t;s),p(t,s))\Phi$ with $\Phi$ as in step 1.1, and the phase $e^{iS/\hbar}$ is irrelevant to means and centered norms; step 1.2 applied to the unit vector $\Phi$ (unit by unitarity of the free evolution) and step 1.1 give $$\langle Q\rangle(t)=\sqrt2\ell\operatorname{Re}\bigl(ze^{-i\omega(t-s)}\bigr)+q(t;s),\qquad \langle P\rangle(t)=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}\bigl(ze^{-i\omega(t-s)}\bigr)+p(t;s),$$ with spreads $\ell/\sqrt2$ and $\hbar/(\ell\sqrt2)$ and product $\hbar/2$. These are clauses (a) and (b).

[Undriven check and scope] For $f\equiv0$ the classical zero-data solution is $q\equiv p\equiv0$ (uniqueness of the linear initial-value problem), so clause (a) reduces to the free rotation, as in [L2]; the computation used only the declared model and its cited mathematics, and no laboratory, damping or measurement claim entered. These are clauses (c) and (d).
